title: Higher direct image restriction along an arbitrary open immersion
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], and $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-cohomology]. For an open immersion $g:T\prime\to T$ and its cartesian base change square with $g\prime:X\prime\to X$ and $f\prime:X\prime\to T\prime$, for every $q\ge0$ there is an isomorphism $R^q f\prime_* (g\prime{}^*\mathcal F)\cong (R^q f_*\mathcal F)|_{T\prime}$. No quasi-coherence or finiteness assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 08FE, together with Tag 01E1(1), bounded-below injective-resolution case; ordinary module pushforward and exact restriction

proof.text: Factor an open immersion j through its open image. Restriction to that image sends an injective module to an injective module, by applying the existing restricted-resolution theorem to the trivial resolution of the injective module. The over-site equivalence and the explicit restriction equivalence associated with the isomorphism onto the image preserve injectives. Transport through overFunctorEquiv and restriction-composition isomorphisms. Exactness of open restriction follows from the existing preservesLimitsOfSize_restrictFunctor and its left-adjoint colimit preservation.

The pullback square makes gprime an open immersion. On an open W of Tprime the identity gprime image fprime inverse W = f inverse g image W is the Mathlib image_preimage_eq_preimage_image_of_isPullback theorem. Compose the module pushforward functors, then use pushforwardCongr2 with that equality. To check the scalar maps, compose with the invertible gprime.appIso.hom. Rewrite appIso_homprime and appLE_comp_appLE: both maps are the appLE of the two equal composite scheme morphisms in the square. Thus pushforward followed by restriction is naturally isomorphic to restriction followed by pushforward.

Restrict an injective resolution I of F termwise to Xprime, with the augmentation given by singleMapHomologicalComplex and the restriction of I. Exactness and injective preservation give a resolution J. Apply the underived comparison termwise. Take homology, commute it with exact restriction on T, and compose the two isoRightDerivedObj comparisons. Finally use restrictFunctorIsoPullback on F to obtain the stated domain. This includes degree zero and the empty open, with the same argument.

lean.statement:
theorem nonempty_higherDirectImage_iso_restrict {T' X' : Scheme.{u}} (g : T' ⟶ T)
    [IsOpenImmersion g] (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ T') [HasInjectiveResolutions X'.Modules]
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (q : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((higherDirectImage f' q).obj ((Modules.pullback g').obj ℱ) ≅
      ((higherDirectImage f q).obj ℱ).restrict g)
